references.text: Describes the same ritual where the anointed priest brings the blood into the tent of meeting and sprinkles it before the veil and on the altar of incense.
On the Day of Atonement, the high priest brings the blood into the Most Holy Place, a parallel to the anointed priest bringing the blood into the tent of meeting.
Refers to the anointing of Aaron and his sons for priestly service, which provides the background for the expression 'the anointed priest' (הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ).
Refers to the tent of meeting (אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) where the priest was to serve before the Lord's presence.
Confirms that any sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting must not be eaten but burned with fire.
Explains how the high priest under the old covenant entered the second room with blood, which he offered for himself and the people's sins—a typology pointing to Christ.
Christ entered the holy place once for all, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood—the fulfillment of what the anointed priest did with the bull's blood.
